paper_title: NExtLong Toward Effective Long-Context Training without Long Documents
caption: NExtLong reduces the model's dependence on proximal text. We calculated the degree of dependence on proximal text (the last third of the text) for different methods when completing the LongQA task. It can be observed that NExtLong significantly reduces the model's dependence on proximal text.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the short-dependence attention weight for five different methods—Standard, ICLM, KNN, Quest, and NExtLong—when completing the LongQA task, with the y-axis representing the attention weight on a scale from 0.80 to 0.90. The x-axis displays the methods, and the bars, all in light blue, represent the computed short-dependence attention weight for each method. The Standard method has the highest attention weight, at approximately 0.868, followed closely by KNN and Quest, both around 0.865. The ICLM method shows a slightly lower weight, at about 0.855, while NExtLong exhibits the lowest attention weight, at approximately 0.835. This visual data supports the claim that NExtLong significantly reduces the model's dependence on proximal text, as it assigns the lowest attention weight to the last third of the text compared to the other methods. The chart clearly demonstrates that NExtLong's approach results in a more balanced or distributed attention pattern, minimizing reliance on the most recent context.
